bibliographic.authors: Agarwal, S., Rodriguez, M. A., & Buyya, R.
bibliographic.title: Dynamic Configuration of Serverless Computing Functions: A Systematic Literature Review

surveys.problem: Examines how Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) platforms dynamically tune runtime configurations—primarily memory allocation, concurrency limits, timeouts, and placement—after deployment to avoid over-provisioning cost and SLA violations under fluctuating workloads.
taxonomy_dimensions: Optimization objectives (cost, latency/SLA, resource utilization, sustainability)
Sustainability-oriented dynamic FaaS configuration strategies (Section 3.4.3)
Decision-making paradigm across 40 surveyed dynamic FaaS configuration techniques (Table 2, p. 28)
Cloud vs. edge FaaS deployment scope and provider characteristics (e.g., AWS Lambda market context)
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: Commercial serverless FaaS platforms including AWS Lambda
CPU-centric FaaS function benchmarks and dynamic configuration traces evaluated in the 40 surveyed studies (Table 2, p. 28)
key_quantitative_results: Catalogs 40 dynamic FaaS configuration techniques in Table 2 (p. 28), of which only 4 target sustainability-oriented objectives (Section 3.4.3).
Notes AWS Lambda holds over 50% serverless market share (p. 7).
Full-text body keyword audit (excluding refs p. 31+): serverless=149, carbon=18, slo=14, cold start=13, gpu=1, llm=1, prefill=0, decode=0, disaggregat=0, kv cache=0, embodied=0.
limitations: Focuses overwhelmingly on stateless CPU FaaS memory/concurrency tuning (gpu=1, llm=1) rather than multi-GB GPU model checkpoints.
Zero coverage of phase disaggregation (prefill=0, decode=0, disaggregat=0), KV-cache migration (kv cache=0), or hardware embodied carbon (embodied=0).
relevance_to_rqs: RQ1: Demonstrates how sparsely sustainability appears in serverless configuration literature (only 4/40 techniques) and proves zero intersection with LLM phase disaggregation.
RQ3: Motivates extending dynamic configuration beyond CPU memory sizing toward carbon-aware keep-alive window control for GPU LLM serverless endpoints.

bibliographic.authors: Alam, S., Ramzan, M. A., Zubair, M., Ullah, U., Ziaullah, Nawaz, R., & Ullah, R.
bibliographic.title: AI-driven resource management in cloud and serverless computing: a systematic review

surveys.problem: Synthesizes artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques applied to resource provisioning, autoscaling, scheduling, and energy optimization across cloud and serverless environments.
taxonomy_dimensions: PRISMA-2020 systematic literature review screening process
Learning paradigm (e.g., reinforcement learning vs. supervised/metaheuristic schedulers)
Evaluation methodology (simulation vs. testbed, Table 1, p. 9)
Target optimization metric (latency, cost, energy efficiency, carbon awareness)
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: Simulation frameworks—predominantly CloudSim—used across 70% (44 of 63) of retained primary studies (Table 1, p. 9)
key_quantitative_results: Screens 485 candidate papers down to 63 retained primary studies via PRISMA-2020.
Reinforcement learning represents 40% of AI-driven scheduling approaches.
Reported mean improvements across subsets: ~45% latency reduction (10 studies), 32% cost reduction (6 studies), and 35% energy reduction (16 studies).
Table 1 (p. 9) shows 70% (44/63) rely on simulation (e.g., CloudSim), while only 4/63 (6.3%) incorporate carbon awareness.
Full-text body keyword audit (excluding refs p. 22+): energy=54, serverless=42, carbon=37, cold start=9, gpu=0, llm=0, embodied=0, prefill=0, decode=0.
limitations: Contains zero coverage of GPU workloads or LLM inference semantics (gpu=0, llm=0, prefill=0, decode=0) and zero embodied carbon modeling (embodied=0).
Confirms simulation dominance (70% CloudSim) for macro-scheduling without LLM KV-cache or phase-level modeling.
relevance_to_rqs: RQ1: Quantifies the scarcity of carbon-aware schedulers (4/63 = 6.3%) in broader AI cloud/serverless management and establishes precedent for discrete-event simulation validation.

bibliographic.authors: Bai, G., Chai, Z., Ling, C., Wang, S., Lu, J., Zhang, N., Shi, T., Yu, Z., Zhu, M., Zhang, Y., Yang, C., Cheng, Y., & Zhao, L. (14 authors)
bibliographic.title: Beyond Efficiency: A Systematic Survey of Resource-Efficient Large Language Models

surveys.problem: Provides a comprehensive lifecycle review of methods reducing compute, memory, network, storage, and energy bottlenecks across LLM pretraining, fine-tuning, and inference.
taxonomy_dimensions: Five-resource lifecycle taxonomy (compute, memory, energy, network, storage; Section 2.2, p. 9)
Model-level compression (pruning, quantization such as AWQ, distillation)
System-level serving optimizations and energy/carbon accounting formulas including SCI (Sections 7-9, pp. 31-41)
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: 8 standardized LLM evaluation benchmarks surveyed across efficiency comparisons
key_quantitative_results: Details energy-to-carbon conversion via PUE x kWh x gCO2eq/kWh and the Software Carbon Intensity (SCI) metric (Sections 7-9, pp. 31-41).
Reports up to 60% structural pruning (p. 23) and AWQ quantization protecting 1% salient weights (p. 24).
Full-text body keyword audit (excluding refs p. 44+): energy=36, carbon=10, kv=4, ttft=2, prefill=0, disaggregat=0, serverless=0, cold start=0, embodied=0.
limitations: Emphasizes model compression and intra-node algorithmic efficiency rather than cluster-wide P/D phase disaggregation (prefill=0, disaggregat=0) or serverless cold-start management (serverless=0, cold start=0).
Omits GPU embodied carbon amortization across heterogeneous node lifetimes (embodied=0).
relevance_to_rqs: RQ1: Establishes LLM energy/carbon/SCI accounting taxonomy while revealing absent coverage of phase-disaggregated and serverless carbon scheduling.
RQ2, RQ4: Supports SCI-aligned operational carbon accounting equations and LLM simulator benchmarking.

bibliographic.title: Toward Green AI: A Methodological Survey of the Scientific Literature

surveys.problem: Contrasts compute-maximizing 'Red AI' practices against sustainable 'Green AI' methodologies, synthesizing tools, carbon estimators, and architectural strategies across the ML literature.
taxonomy_dimensions: Red AI vs. Green AI methodological dichotomy (Table 1, p. 3)
Carbon measurement and estimation methodologies for neural architectures
Case-study carbon footprints across foundation/transformer models (Tables 5-8, pp. 16-18)
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: Case studies and published footprint measurements for BERT, GPT, and PaLM foundation models (Tables 5-8, pp. 16-18)
key_quantitative_results: Summarizes BERT, GPT, and PaLM energy/carbon case studies in Tables 5-8 (pp. 16-18).
Synthesizes reported 25-50% carbon savings achievable through renewable-powered regions and more efficient model architectures.
Full-text body keyword audit (excluding refs p. 23+): energy=125, carbon=49, gpu=33, slo=9, llm=4, decode=2, embodied=0, serverless=0, cold start=0, prefill=0, disaggregat=0, kv cache=0.
limitations: Focuses heavily on training footprints and static model-level Green AI guidelines rather than SLO-constrained online inference phase scheduling (prefill=0, disaggregat=0, kv cache=0).
Lacks serverless cold-start dynamics (serverless=0, cold start=0) and embodied hardware amortization (embodied=0).
relevance_to_rqs: RQ1: Anchors the foundational Red-vs-Green AI taxonomy and documents early training-centric bias in cloud AI sustainability literature.

bibliographic.authors: Besozzi, V., Della Bartola, M., Dazzi, P., & Danelutto, M.
bibliographic.title: A Systematic Literature Review on Serverless Computing: Trends, Platforms, and Future Directions

surveys.problem: Maps the evolution of serverless computing platforms, architectural disaggregation trends, hardware accelerator integration, and operational challenges via a large-scale systematic literature review.
taxonomy_dimensions: SLR plus backward/forward snowballing methodology (p. 8)
Serverless platform architectures and open-source/commercial stacks (Tables 1-8, pp. 4-19)
Hardware accelerator support and hardware-level resource disaggregation
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: Production and open-source serverless platforms surveyed in Tables 1-8 (pp. 4-19): Apache OpenWhisk, Knative, AWS Lambda, Huawei Cloud
key_quantitative_results: Retains 122 primary papers out of 579 candidates via systematic screening and snowballing (p. 8).
Reports 29.5% of surveyed serverless work addresses hardware accelerators and 28.6% examines hardware disaggregation (p. 9).
Explicitly identifies geo-distributed carbon-aware serverless AI execution as an open future direction.
Full-text body keyword audit (excluding refs p. 39+): serverless=596, gpu=88, cold start=46, disaggregat=44, energy=25, slo=6, carbon=2, embodied=0, llm=0, kv=0, prefill=0.
limitations: Hardware disaggregation denotes CPU/memory/GPU pool disaggregation rather than LLM prefill/decode phase disaggregation (llm=0, kv=0, prefill=0).
Minimal carbon coverage (carbon=2) and zero embodied carbon modeling (embodied=0).
relevance_to_rqs: RQ1: Demonstrates strong interest in serverless GPUs (gpu=88) and hardware disaggregation (disaggregat=44) alongside virtually absent carbon routing (carbon=2).
RQ3: Explicitly motivates our geo-distributed, carbon-aware serverless GPU LLM keep-alive investigation.

bibliographic.authors: Chen, X., Yu, H., Ni, W., Niyato, D., Zhang, R., Wang, X., Zhang, S., & Xu, S.
bibliographic.title: Energy-Efficient Agentic AI: A Survey of Methods, Architectures, and Future Directions

surveys.problem: Surveys energy consumption drivers and optimization mechanisms across perception-reasoning-action cycles in edge, 6G, and cloud-assisted agentic AI systems powered by LLMs.
taxonomy_dimensions: Three-stage Perception-Reasoning-Action energy breakdown
KV-cache compression, prompt pruning, and token-level hardware/power scheduling techniques (Tables 4-7, pp. 13-22)
Edge/6G offload and future grid-aware carbon routing directions
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: Systems and methods surveyed in Tables 4-7 (pp. 13-22): KIVI (KV quantization), LLMLingua (prompt compression), TAPAS, POLCA
key_quantitative_results: Highlights 640 pJ off-chip DRAM access cost driving KV-cache memory-wall energy and 50-60% sparsity bounds for OPT-175B (p. 10).
Catalogs KV/prompt/power-control mechanisms (KIVI, LLMLingua, TAPAS, POLCA) across Tables 4-7 (pp. 13-22).
Explicitly flags geographic carbon routing and real-time carbon-intensity APIs as open future work.
Full-text body keyword audit (excluding refs p. 28+): energy=331, llm=108, gpu=38, kv=24, carbon=13, prefill=9, decode=6, disaggregat=0, serverless=0, slo=0, embodied=0.
limitations: Focused on edge/6G agentic loops rather than multi-region cloud data-center P/D disaggregation (disaggregat=0), strict cloud serving SLOs (slo=0), or serverless FaaS cold starts (serverless=0).
Zero treatment of hardware embodied carbon (embodied=0).
relevance_to_rqs: RQ1, RQ2: Reinforces the memory-vs-compute energy asymmetry between prefill and decode and directly names geographic carbon-intensity API routing as an unresolved research gap.

bibliographic.authors: Golec, M., Walia, G. K., Kumar, M., Cuadrado, F., Gill, S. S., & Uhlig, S.
bibliographic.title: Cold Start Latency in Serverless Computing: A Systematic Review, Taxonomy, and Future Directions

surveys.problem: Conducts a systematic review of serverless cold-start latency causes, mitigation mechanisms (pre-warming, snapshotting, lightweight isolation), and evaluation platforms.
taxonomy_dimensions: Cold-start mitigation category (keep-alive/pre-warming, checkpoint/snapshot restore, runtime/sandbox optimization)
Evaluated FaaS platforms and experiment counts (Tables 4-5, pp. 24-27)
Energy side effects of warm container retention (Section 6.1)
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: Apache OpenWhisk (34.37% of core studies) and AWS Lambda (29.03% of core studies) across Tables 4-5 (pp. 24-27)
key_quantitative_results: Reviews >100 candidate papers and synthesizes 32 core studies in Tables 4-5 (pp. 24-27).
OpenWhisk (34.37%) and AWS Lambda (29.03%) dominate evaluation platforms.
Section 6.1 explicitly highlights idle energy waste incurred by static warm keep-alive pools.
Full-text body keyword audit (excluding refs p. 37+): cold start=292, serverless=256, energy=10, slo=3, gpu=1, carbon=0, embodied=0, llm=0, kv=0.
limitations: Zero coverage of carbon intensity (carbon=0), embodied carbon (embodied=0), LLM inference (llm=0), or KV-cache state (kv=0), with only 1 GPU mention.
Does not quantify the idle-vs-reload carbon crossover on high-TDP accelerators hosting multi-GB LLM checkpoints.
relevance_to_rqs: RQ1, RQ3: Establishes the keep-alive latency-vs-idle-energy trade-off conceptually while leaving multi-GB GPU LLM checkpoints and grid carbon intensity unaddressed.

bibliographic.authors: Hewage, T. B., Ilager, S., Read, M. R., Arroba, P., & Buyya, R.
bibliographic.title: Carbon-Aware Computing for Latency-Sensitive Cloud Applications: A Comprehensive Survey

surveys.problem: Investigates how latency-sensitive interactive cloud and serverless services—which cannot rely on coarse temporal batch shifting—reduce both operational and embodied carbon under strict tail-latency constraints.
taxonomy_dimensions: Operational vs. embodied carbon accounting for interactive workloads (Table 1, p. 8)
Spatial/geographical routing vs. resource right-sizing and hardware lifecycle extension
Latency-constrained cloud, CDN, and serverless carbon-aware frameworks (Tables 2-3, p. 21)
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: Latency-sensitive carbon-aware systems cataloged on pp. 10-21: LACE-RL (p. 21), Caribou (Gsteiger et al. [17], pp. 13-16), Chien et al. [11] geo-distributed GenAI, Murillo et al. [30] CDN routing (p. 10)
key_quantitative_results: Reviews LACE-RL for serverless scheduling (p. 21) and Caribou [17] for geo-distributed serverless DAGs (pp. 13-16).
Cites Murillo et al. [30] showing 60 ms CDN routing slack enables >60% operational carbon reduction (p. 10).
Synthesizes operational and embodied carbon optimization axes across Table 1 (p. 8) and Tables 2-3 (p. 21).

Full-text body keyword audit (excluding refs p. 26+): carbon=281, energy=171, embodied=61, slo=40, serverless=21, operational carbon=11, cold start=7, gpu=2, llm=0, prefill=0, decode=0, kv=0, disaggregat=0.
limitations: Does not address LLM inference phase internals, KV-cache migration overhead, or prefill/decode hardware heterogeneity (llm=0, prefill=0, decode=0, kv=0, disaggregat=0).
Minimal GPU focus (gpu=2) despite rich operational+embodied carbon taxonomy.
relevance_to_rqs: RQ1: Strongest holistic operational+embodied carbon survey in the corpus, showing zero intersection with LLM phase disaggregation.
RQ3, RQ4: Directly informs our spatial carbon routing under TTFT/TPOT slack, serverless LACE-RL/Caribou comparison, and amortized embodied carbon formulation.

bibliographic.authors: Jiang, J., Yang, P., Zhang, R., & Liu, F.
bibliographic.title: A Survey on KV Cache Optimization for Large Language Model Serving
bibliographic.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2026)

surveys.problem: Organizes algorithms and distributed system mechanisms addressing the KV-cache memory capacity, bandwidth, and cross-node transfer bottlenecks in large-scale LLM inference.
taxonomy_dimensions: 3D 'sKis' KV-cache taxonomy (Tables 2-7, pp. 4-8): Execution/Scheduling (OVLP overlapping, HAE hardware-aware execution), Placement/Migration (MHO memory hierarchy offloading, CDO cross-node/distributed offloading), Representation (KVCC compression/clustering, KVRM reuse/management)
Appendix G Tanimoto affinity matrix across mechanism pairs (Tables 11-12, pp. 25-27)
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: LLM serving engines, disaggregated KV engines, and prefix-caching frameworks benchmarked using TTFT, ITL/TPOT, goodput, and energy (Joules/token)
key_quantitative_results: Identifies >=70% high-prevalence technique combinations across the 3D sKis space (p. 8) and reports Tanimoto co-occurrence scores in Appendix G (Tables 11-12, pp. 25-27).
Explicitly recommends reporting Joules/token alongside TTFT, ITL, and SLO goodput in future KV-cache evaluations.
Full-text body keyword audit (excluding refs p. 10+): kv=40, llm=40, gpu=32, decode=12, energy=12, prefill=9, disaggregat=9, slo=6, carbon=0, embodied=0, serverless=0, cold start=0.
limitations: Zero treatment of grid carbon intensity, operational carbon, embodied hardware emissions, or serverless cold-start retention (carbon=0, embodied=0, serverless=0, cold start=0).
Short main body (9 pages before references) focused purely on intra-cluster performance and raw energy.
relevance_to_rqs: RQ1, RQ2: Establishes exact KV-cache transfer, compression, and prefix-reuse mechanisms plus the recommendation to measure Joules/token alongside TTFT/ITL/SLO goodput.

bibliographic.authors: Li, B., Jiang, Y., Gadepally, V., & Tiwari, D.
bibliographic.title: LLM Inference Serving: Survey of Recent Advances and Opportunities
bibliographic.venue: IEEE High Performance Extreme Computing Conference (HPEC 2024)

taxonomy_dimensions: Continuous batching and memory management (Orca, vLLM, Sarathi)
Prefill/decode disaggregation and KV sharing (Splitwise, DistServe, MemServe, LoongServe)
Elastic/serverless and early carbon-aware inference (SpotServe, ServerlessLLM, Sprout)
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: Catalogs 10 canonical serving systems (Orca, vLLM, Sarathi, Splitwise, DistServe, MemServe, LoongServe, SpotServe, ServerlessLLM, Sprout) within 8 pages
key_quantitative_results: Maps early prefill-decode disaggregation systems (Splitwise, DistServe) alongside serverless serving (ServerlessLLM) and token-generation carbon control (Sprout).

limitations: Brief 6-page main body with only a single passing mention of carbon (carbon=1 via Sprout) and zero embodied carbon analysis (embodied=0).

bibliographic.authors: Miao, X., Oliaro, G., Zhang, Z., Cheng, X., Jin, H., Chen, T., & Jia, Z.
bibliographic.title: Towards Efficient Generative Large Language Model Serving: A Survey from Algorithms to Systems

taxonomy_dimensions: End-to-end algorithms-to-systems LLM serving taxonomy (Figure 1, p. 5)
Runtime architecture matrix spanning colocation, P/D disaggregation, and serverless loading (Table 2)
Production workload characteristics and trace evaluation (BurstGPT and Azure LLM traces, pp. 11-18)
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: LLM serving engines in Table 2: vLLM, Sarathi, Splitwise, DistServe, Mooncake, ServerlessLLM
Production traces discussed on pp. 11-18: BurstGPT and Azure LLM inference traces
key_quantitative_results: Compares colocation, disaggregated P/D, and serverless checkpoint-loading systems in Table 2 and characterizes BurstGPT and Azure traces (pp. 11-18).
Explicitly states that the survey's primary scope is latency/throughput performance rather than energy or carbon optimization.
Full-text body keyword audit (excluding refs p. 21+): carbon=2, energy=2, embodied=0.
limitations: Explicitly excludes carbon-aware scheduling, renewable grid tracking, and embodied hardware carbon from its analytical framework (carbon=2, energy=2, embodied=0).

RQ2, RQ3: Guides baseline engine comparisons (vLLM/Sarathi colocated, Splitwise/DistServe/Mooncake disaggregated, ServerlessLLM) and Azure trace justification.

bibliographic.title: A Survey of LLM Inference Systems from a Data Management Perspective

surveys.problem: Reframes LLM inference serving through data-management abstractions: KV-cache storage hierarchies, prefix indexing, disaggregated prefill-decode dataflows, and serverless elasticity.
taxonomy_dimensions: Serving runtime and dataflow comparison across colocation, sync/async P/D disaggregation, and serverless (Tables 3-4, pp. 18-21)
Synchronous vs. asynchronous prefill-decode KV transfer pipelines (Figure 20)
Serverless GPU model state transfer and cold-start mitigation (e.g., DeepFlow)
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: Catalogs disaggregated and serverless LLM serving runtimes including DeepFlow across Tables 3-4 (pp. 18-21)
key_quantitative_results: Distinguishes synchronous vs. asynchronous P/D KV-cache disaggregation architectures (Figure 20) and compares runtimes in Tables 3-4 (pp. 18-21).
Full-text body keyword audit (excluding refs p. 22+): prefill=29, decode=28, kv=24, disaggregat=12, serverless=6, cold start=3, carbon=0, energy=0, embodied=0.
limitations: Zero coverage of energy consumption, operational grid carbon, or embodied carbon in body text (carbon=0, energy=0, embodied=0).
relevance_to_rqs: RQ1: Confirms complete absence of energy/carbon optimization even in recent 2025 disaggregated-serving reviews.
RQ2, RQ3: Clarifies sync vs. async KV transfer semantics in disaggregated routers and serverless GPU checkpoint movement.

bibliographic.title: From Engines to Control Planes: Evidence-Weighted Taxonomy of Distributed LLM Serving

surveys.problem: Critiques single-engine optimizations and proposes a five-stage architectural taxonomy with evidence weighting to evaluate Kubernetes-native distributed LLM control planes (e.g., llm-d).
taxonomy_dimensions: Evidence-tier classification Tiers A-D separating production measurements from simulation/prototype claims (Table 1, p. 3)
Five-stage serving expansion from engine batching to control-plane P/D and KV routing (Figure 1, p. 4)
Analytical KV-cache transfer vs. prefill recomputation crossover threshold (Equation 1, p. 4)
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: Distributed LLM control planes and benchmarks: vLLM engine, llm-d v0.8-v0.9, Splitwise, DistServe, Mooncake, Llumnix
key_quantitative_results: Formulates Equation (1) (p. 4): T_transfer(S,i,j) + T_queue(j) < min{T_queue(i), T_recompute(S,j)} governing when KV migration outperforms local/remote recomputation.

Synthesizes landmark disaggregation speedups under evidence Tiers A-D (Table 1, p. 3): Splitwise (1.4x throughput at iso-cost, 2.35x at iso-power), DistServe (7.4x rate / 12.6x tighter SLO), Mooncake (525% throughput in simulation / 75% in real testbed), and Llumnix (36% cost reduction).
Includes only 1 carbon reference in the entire review, with embodied=0 and serverless=0.
limitations: Virtually omits carbon intensity (1 reference), serverless GPU cold-start lifecycles (serverless=0), and embodied hardware amortization (embodied=0).
Transfer-vs-recompute inequality (Eq. 1) optimizes latency alone without weighting operational energy or regional carbon intensity.
relevance_to_rqs: RQ1: Demonstrates the state of the art in control-plane disaggregation taxonomies and exposes its blind spot on operational/embodied carbon and serverless cold starts.
RQ2: Provides Equation (1) directly as the structural foundation for our Carbon+KV-Aware Hybrid Router decision rule (extended with regional energy and carbon weights).

bibliographic.authors: Yang, J., Saad, Z., Wu, J., Niu, X., Leung, H., & Drew, S.
bibliographic.title: Carbon-Aware Container Scheduling in Cloud Computing: A Systematic Review

surveys.problem: Conducts a PRISMA systematic review of carbon-aware scheduling, telemetry, and autoscaling techniques for containerized Kubernetes and serverless microservices in multi-region clouds.
taxonomy_dimensions: PRISMA dual-layer taxonomy distinguishing carbon-awareness mechanisms and scheduling granularity (Table 1, p. 3)
Temporal shifting vs. spatial migration vs. resource scaling frameworks (Tables 2-5, pp. 10-13)
Carbon telemetry stacks and Software Carbon Intensity (SCI) normalization (Section 6.2)
datasets_and_simulators_surveyed: Carbon schedulers and energy monitors (Tables 2-5, pp. 10-13): CarbonScaler (-51% carbon), Caspian (-33% carbon), GreenCourier, CASA, Kepler, KubeWatt
key_quantitative_results: Cites US data-center electricity demand projections growing from 176 TWh to 580 TWh by 2028 (p. 5).
Reports container carbon-scheduler reductions including CarbonScaler (-51%) and Caspian (-33%) (Tables 2-5, pp. 10-13).
Adopts Software Carbon Intensity (SCI) accounting (Section 6.2).

Full-text body keyword audit (excluding refs p. 30+): carbon=319, energy=255, serverless=25, gpu=20, slo=9, llm=3, cold start=2, operational carbon=1, embodied=0, prefill=0, decode=0, disaggregat=0, kv=0.
limitations: Focuses on stateless CPU/microservice Kubernetes pods and serverless functions; zero coverage of LLM prefill/decode disaggregation or KV-cache state (prefill=0, decode=0, disaggregat=0, kv=0).
Zero modeling of embodied hardware amortization across asymmetric GPU lifetimes (embodied=0) and minimal LLM coverage (llm=3).

RQ2, RQ3: Motivates extending container-level spatial carbon scaling (e.g., GreenCourier, CarbonScaler) into phase-aware P/D and serverless GPU checkpoint routing.
